text: 有的人骑在人民头上；有的人俯下身子给人民当牛马
pinyin: yǒu de rén qí zài rén mín tóu shàng, yǒu de rén fǔ xià shēn zi gěi rén mín dāng niú mǎ
literal: some · people · ride · on · people's · heads, some · people · bend · body · for · people · serve as · ox · horse
natural: some ride on the people's backs; others stoop to serve them like beasts of burden

meaning.en: Zang Kejia's contrast between those who lord it over the people and those who humbly serve them.
meaning.zh: 臧克家的对比：有的人凌驾于人民之上，有的人甘愿俯身为人民服务。

equivalents: lord it over the people vs. serve the people
masters versus servants of the people

examples.zh: 他引用臧克家的诗：“有的人骑在人民头上；有的人俯下身子给人民当牛马。”
examples.en: He quoted Zang Kejia: 'Some ride on the people's heads; others bend down to serve them as beasts of burden.'

examples.zh: 评价官员，不妨想想“有的人骑在人民头上；有的人俯下身子给人民当牛马”这两种人。
examples.en: In judging officials, think of the two kinds in the line 'some ride on the people's heads; others bend down to serve them'.

story.en: Zang Kejia (1905-2004) wrote 'Some People' (《有的人》) in November 1949 to mark the 13th anniversary of Lu Xun's death, contrasting those who live for themselves with those who live for the people.
story.zh: 臧克家（1905—2004）1949年11月为纪念鲁迅逝世十三周年作《有的人》，对比为己而活者与为人民而活者。

usage.en: In the poem a quoted cry (“呵，我多伟大！”) comes between the two lines; they are usually quoted together as here. Written in 1949 for the anniversary of Lu Xun's death. Often quoted in discussions of officials and public service; the poem opens '有的人活着，他已经死了；有的人死了，他还活着'.
usage.zh: 原诗两句之间还有一句引语“呵，我多伟大！”，引用时多连在一起。作于1949年，纪念鲁迅逝世。常用于谈论官员和公共服务。全诗开头是“有的人活着，他已经死了；有的人死了，他还活着”。

text: 五岭逶迤腾细浪，乌蒙磅礴走泥丸
pinyin: wǔ lǐng wēi yí téng xì làng, wū méng páng bó zǒu ní wán
literal: Five Ridges · winding · churn · fine · waves, Wumeng · mighty · roll · mud · pellets
natural: the Five Ridges ripple like small waves; the mighty Wumeng rolls like mud balls

meaning.en: Mao's line on the Long March: mountain ranges that look like ripples and mud pellets to the marching Red Army.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东写长征：五岭、乌蒙这样的大山，在红军眼中不过是细浪和泥丸。

equivalents: mountains as mere ripples
making light of towering obstacles

examples.zh: “五岭逶迤腾细浪，乌蒙磅礴走泥丸”写出了红军藐视困难的气概。
examples.en: 'The Five Ridges ripple like small waves, the mighty Wumeng rolls like mud balls' shows the Red Army's contempt for hardship.

examples.zh: 她在演讲里引用“五岭逶迤腾细浪，乌蒙磅礴走泥丸”，鼓励队员翻过这座山。
examples.en: In her speech she quoted 'the Five Ridges ripple like small waves…' to urge the team over the hill.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote the regulated verse 'The Long March' (《七律·长征》) in October 1935, as the Red Army ended its march; this is the second couplet.
story.zh: 毛泽东1935年10月红军长征即将结束时作《七律·长征》，此为颔联。

usage.en: Quoted to describe treating huge obstacles lightly. 逶迤 is wēi yí (winding). A staple of school textbooks.
usage.zh: 用来形容把巨大的困难看得很轻。“逶迤”读 wēi yí。是课本里的常见名句。

text: 西风烈，长空雁叫霜晨月
pinyin: xī fēng liè, cháng kōng yàn jiào shuāng chén yuè
literal: west · wind · fierce, long · sky · geese · cry · frost · morning · moon
natural: the west wind is fierce; geese cry across the sky under the frosty morning moon

meaning.en: Mao's opening of his Loushan Pass poem: a bleak, stirring scene of autumn wind and a frosty dawn moon.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《忆秦娥·娄山关》的开头：西风猛烈，霜晨月下雁声长鸣，景象苍凉而雄壮。

equivalents: a fierce wind under a frosty morning moon
the bleak dawn before the battle

examples.zh: “西风烈，长空雁叫霜晨月”，一开篇就是萧瑟的秋景。
examples.en: 'The west wind is fierce, geese cry in the sky under the frosty morning moon': the poem opens on a bleak autumn scene.

examples.zh: 清晨的山口寒风刺骨，他不由得想起“西风烈，长空雁叫霜晨月”。
examples.en: At dawn the cold wind at the pass cut to the bone, and he thought of 'the west wind is fierce…'.

origin.source: 毛泽东《忆秦娥·娄山关》（1935年）

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote the lyric 'Loushan Pass' (《忆秦娥·娄山关》) in February 1935, after the Red Army's battle for the pass in Guizhou during the Long March.
story.zh: 毛泽东1935年2月红军长征中在贵州娄山关战斗之后作《忆秦娥·娄山关》。

usage.en: The following line repeats the last three characters (霜晨月), a feature of the 忆秦娥 form. Quoted for cold, stirring dawn scenes.
usage.zh: 下一句重复“霜晨月”三字，是《忆秦娥》词牌的特点。常用来写寒冷而雄壮的清晨景象。

pinyin: cāng shān rú hǎi, cán yáng rú xuè
literal: dark · mountains · like · sea, remaining · sun · like · blood
natural: the green mountains are a sea; the setting sun is blood

meaning.en: Mao's closing image in his Loushan Pass poem: endless dark mountains and a blood-red sunset after battle.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《忆秦娥·娄山关》的结尾：群山连绵如海，残阳红如鲜血。

equivalents: a sea of mountains under a blood-red sunset

examples.zh: 站在山顶，只见苍山如海，残阳如血。
examples.en: Standing on the summit, he saw nothing but a sea of mountains and a blood-red setting sun.

examples.zh: 这幅画题为“苍山如海，残阳如血”，取自毛泽东的词。
examples.en: The painting is titled 'Sea of Mountains, Blood-red Sun', taken from Mao's lyric.

origin.source: 毛泽东《忆秦娥·娄山关》（1935年）

story.en: These are the last two lines of the lyric written after the battle at Loushan Pass in 1935.
story.zh: 这是1935年娄山关战斗后所作词的结尾两句。

usage.en: Often used on its own to describe a vast, solemn mountain sunset or a moving historical scene. 血 is read xuè in this literary use.
usage.zh: 常单独引用，形容辽阔壮烈的山中落日，或沉重的历史场景。这里“血”读 xuè。

pinyin: tiān gāo yún dàn, wàng duàn nán fēi yàn
literal: sky · high · clouds · thin, gaze · to the end · south · flying · geese
natural: under a high sky and thin clouds, I watch the geese fly south until they vanish

meaning.en: Mao's opening of his Mount Liupan poem: a clear autumn sky and the gaze following geese heading south.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东《清平乐·六盘山》的开头：秋高云淡，目送南飞的大雁远去。

equivalents: a clear autumn sky and geese flying south

examples.zh: “天高云淡，望断南飞雁”，下一句就是“不到长城非好汉”。
examples.en: 'Under a high sky, thin clouds, I watch the south-flying geese': the next line is 'he who has not reached the Great Wall is no true man'.

examples.zh: 秋天登上山顶，他念起“天高云淡，望断南飞雁”。
examples.en: Climbing to the summit in autumn, he recited 'a high sky, thin clouds, watching the south-flying geese'.

origin.source: 毛泽东《清平乐·六盘山》（1935年）

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'Mount Liupan' (《清平乐·六盘山》) in October 1935, near the end of the Long March.
story.zh: 毛泽东1935年10月长征即将结束时作《清平乐·六盘山》。

usage.en: The first half of the lyric whose next line is 不到长城非好汉. Do not confuse with the four-character idiom 天高云淡 (a clear autumn sky), which has its own entry.
usage.zh: 此词下一句是“不到长城非好汉”。注意与四字成语“天高云淡”（形容秋日晴朗）区别，后者另有词条。

pinyin: zhàn dì huáng huā fèn wài xiāng
literal: battle · ground · yellow · flowers · especially · fragrant
natural: the chrysanthemums on the battlefield smell all the sweeter

meaning.en: Mao's image of flowers on the battlefield that seem especially fragrant: hardship and struggle make beauty richer.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东写战场上的菊花格外芳香：在斗争中，美好的事物更显得可贵。

equivalents: flowers smell sweeter on the battlefield

examples.zh: “战地黄花分外香”，写出了革命者乐观的情怀。
examples.en: 'The battlefield chrysanthemums smell especially sweet' expresses the revolutionary's optimism.

examples.zh: 重阳登高时，老先生吟起“战地黄花分外香”。
examples.en: Climbing the hill on the Double Ninth, the old gentleman chanted 'the battlefield chrysanthemums smell especially sweet'.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote the lyric 'Double Ninth' (《采桑子·重阳》) in October 1929 on the festival, during the Jinggangshan–Fujian campaigns.
story.zh: 毛泽东1929年重阳节作《采桑子·重阳》。

usage.en: Quoted on the Double Ninth Festival (重阳) and when praising cheer in hard conditions. 分 is fèn here. The preceding lines are 人生易老天难老，岁岁重阳。今又重阳。
usage.zh: 常在重阳节和赞美艰苦环境中的乐观时引用。“分”读 fèn。上文是“人生易老天难老，岁岁重阳。今又重阳”。

text: 更立西江石壁，截断巫山云雨，高峡出平湖
pinyin: gèng lì xī jiāng shí bì, jié duàn wū shān yún yǔ, gāo xiá chū píng hú
literal: further · erect · upper river · stone · wall, cut off · Wushan · clouds · rain, high · gorge · produce · calm · lake
natural: build a stone wall across the western stream, cut off the clouds and rain of Wushan, and a calm lake rises in the high gorge

meaning.en: Mao's vision of damming the Yangtze: a wall across the river and a placid lake in the high gorges.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东设想在长江上筑起大坝，高峡之间出现平静的大湖。

equivalents: a lake in the high gorge
taming the river with a great dam

examples.zh: 三峡大坝建成后，人们常引用“更立西江石壁，截断巫山云雨，高峡出平湖”来形容库区的新景象。
examples.en: After the Three Gorges Dam was finished, 'build a stone wall across the western stream… a calm lake in the high gorge' was often quoted to describe the reservoir.

examples.zh: “更立西江石壁，截断巫山云雨，高峡出平湖”，这是毛泽东对大坝的想象。
examples.en: 'Build a stone wall across the western stream… a calm lake in the high gorge': this was Mao's vision of the dam.

origin.source: 毛泽东《水调歌头·游泳》（1956年）

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'Swimming' (《水调歌头·游泳》) in June 1956 after swimming in the Yangtze at Wuhan; these lines imagine a dam across the Three Gorges.
story.zh: 毛泽东1956年6月在武汉畅游长江后作《水调歌头·游泳》，这几句设想在三峡筑坝。

usage.en: The last phrase 高峡出平湖 is often quoted alone for big dam projects. Written before the Three Gorges Dam was begun (1994).
usage.zh: 末句“高峡出平湖”常单独引用，形容大型水坝工程。作于三峡工程动工（1994年）之前。

text: 神女应无恙，当惊世界殊
pinyin: shén nǚ yīng wú yàng, dāng jīng shì jiè shū
literal: goddess · surely · without · harm, would · be startled · world · different
natural: the Goddess is surely well, but she would be startled by how changed the world is

meaning.en: Mao imagines the Wushan Goddess astonished at how the world has changed.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东设想巫山神女看到世界天翻地覆的变化，该会吃惊。

equivalents: the world has changed beyond recognition

examples.zh: 三十年后重返故乡，他感叹“神女应无恙，当惊世界殊”。
examples.en: Returning to his hometown after thirty years, he sighed 'the Goddess is surely well, but she would be startled at how the world has changed'.

examples.zh: 报道的标题引用了“神女应无恙，当惊世界殊”，来形容这座城市的巨变。
examples.en: The headline quoted 'the Goddess would be startled by how the world has changed' to describe the city's transformation.

origin.source: 毛泽东《水调歌头·游泳》（1956年）

story.en: The last two lines of the lyric 'Swimming': the goddess of Wushan, a figure from Chu legend, would be amazed by the dam and lake.
story.zh: 《水调歌头·游泳》的结尾：楚地传说中的巫山神女，看到大坝和平湖，应当感到惊讶。

usage.en: Often quoted to say that a place has changed greatly. 当 is dāng ('would indeed') here.
usage.zh: 常用来说明一个地方变化巨大。这里“当”读 dāng，意为“应当”。

text: 我失骄杨君失柳，杨柳轻飏直上重霄九
pinyin: wǒ shī jiāo yáng jūn shī liǔ, yáng liǔ qīng yáng zhí shàng chóng xiāo jiǔ
literal: I · lost · proud · poplar, you · lost · willow, poplar · willow · lightly · flutter · straight · up · ninth · heaven
natural: I lost my proud Poplar, you lost your Willow; poplar and willow float lightly up to the ninth heaven

meaning.en: Mao's elegy: he and Li Shuyi each lost a spouse (Yang Kaihui, and Liu Zhixun), whose souls rise to heaven like willow catkins.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东的悼亡词：他与李淑一各自失去了爱人（杨开慧、柳直荀），两人的英魂如杨柳飞絮，直上九天。

equivalents: a lament for loved ones lost in the struggle

examples.zh: “我失骄杨君失柳，杨柳轻飏直上重霄九”是毛泽东写给李淑一的词句，“杨”指杨开慧，“柳”指柳直荀。
examples.en: 'I lost my proud Poplar, you lost your Willow' is from Mao's lyric to Li Shuyi: Poplar is Yang Kaihui, Willow is Liu Zhixun.

examples.zh: 她朗诵了“我失骄杨君失柳，杨柳轻飏直上重霄九”，全场肃然。
examples.en: She recited 'I lost my proud Poplar, you lost your Willow…' and the hall fell silent.

origin.source: 毛泽东《蝶恋花·答李淑一》（1957年）

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'Reply to Li Shuyi' (《蝶恋花·答李淑一》) in May 1957, answering a poem from his friend Li Shuyi.
story.zh: 毛泽东1957年5月作《蝶恋花·答李淑一》，答复友人李淑一的来词。

usage.en: Both Yang Kaihui (Mao's wife, executed 1930) and Liu Zhixun (Li Shuyi's husband, killed 1932) died for the revolution; 杨 also puns on the surname. 重 is chóng, 飏 is yáng. Used in discussing the poem or elegiac contexts.
usage.zh: 杨开慧（毛泽东之妻，1930年牺牲）和柳直荀（李淑一之夫，1932年牺牲）均为革命而死；“杨”“柳”亦是二人姓氏。“重”读 chóng，“飏”读 yáng。多用于谈论此词或悼亡场合。

text: 钟山风雨起苍黄，百万雄师过大江
pinyin: zhōng shān fēng yǔ qǐ cāng huáng, bǎi wàn xióng shī guò dà jiāng
literal: Zhong Mountain · wind · rain · rise · turmoil, hundred · ten thousand · mighty · troops · cross · great · river
natural: wind and rain stir over Zhong Mountain; a million troops cross the great river

meaning.en: Mao's line on the PLA crossing the Yangtze in April 1949: Nanjing is thrown into upheaval as a million troops cross.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东写1949年4月人民解放军渡江：钟山风雨骤起，百万大军横渡长江。

equivalents: a mighty army crosses the river

examples.zh: 纪录片以“钟山风雨起苍黄，百万雄师过大江”开篇，讲述渡江战役。
examples.en: The documentary opens with 'wind and rain stir over Zhong Mountain, a million troops cross the great river' to tell of the Yangtze Crossing Campaign.

examples.zh: 历史课上，老师带着学生读“钟山风雨起苍黄，百万雄师过大江”。
examples.en: In history class the teacher read 'wind and rain stir over Zhong Mountain…' with the students.

origin.source: 毛泽东《七律·人民解放军占领南京》（1949年）

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'The PLA Captures Nanjing' (《七律·人民解放军占领南京》) in April 1949, after the Yangtze crossing and the fall of Nanjing.
story.zh: 毛泽东1949年4月渡江战役、南京解放后作《七律·人民解放军占领南京》。

usage.en: Quoted in histories of the 1949 Yangtze Crossing Campaign. 钟山 is Purple Mountain at Nanjing; 苍黄 means sudden change or upheaval.
usage.zh: 多见于1949年渡江战役的叙述。钟山即南京紫金山；“苍黄”指局势急剧变化。

text: 虎踞龙盘今胜昔，天翻地覆慨而慷
pinyin: hǔ jù lóng pán jīn shèng xī, tiān fān dì fù kǎi ér kāng
literal: tiger · crouch · dragon · coil · now · surpasses · past, heaven · overturn · earth · upset · stirring · and · vigorous
natural: the tiger-crouching, dragon-coiling city is greater now than ever; heaven and earth are overturned, stirring and bold

meaning.en: Mao on the capture of Nanjing: the old capital is better than in the past, and the sweeping change is thrilling.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东写南京解放：古都今日胜过往昔，天地翻覆的巨变令人慷慨激昂。

equivalents: a city greater than ever
a world turned upside down, for the better

examples.zh: “虎踞龙盘今胜昔，天翻地覆慨而慷”，毛泽东这样写南京的新生。
examples.en: 'The tiger-crouching, dragon-coiling city is greater than before; heaven and earth are overturned, stirring and bold': this is how Mao wrote of Nanjing's new start.

examples.zh: 游览中山陵时，导游念起“虎踞龙盘今胜昔，天翻地覆慨而慷”。
examples.en: At the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum the guide recited 'the tiger-crouching, dragon-coiling city is greater now than ever'.

origin.source: 毛泽东《七律·人民解放军占领南京》（1949年）

story.en: The third and fourth lines of the 1949 poem on the capture of Nanjing; 虎踞龙盘 had long been used of Nanjing's mountains and river.
story.zh: 1949年解放南京诗的颈联；“虎踞龙盘”早就用来形容南京的山川形势。

usage.en: 虎踞龙盘 (a strategic, imposing site) is also a chengyu of its own; the full couplet is quoted of Nanjing or of any city transformed. 踞 is jù, 盘 is pán.
usage.zh: “虎踞龙盘”本身也是成语，形容地势险要雄伟；整联多用来写南京或任何焕然一新的城市。

text: 喜看稻菽千重浪，遍地英雄下夕烟
pinyin: xǐ kàn dào shū qiān chóng làng, biàn dì yīng xióng xià xī yān
literal: happily · see · rice · beans · thousand · layers · waves, everywhere · heroes · descend · evening · smoke
natural: glad to see waves of rice and beans in their thousands; heroes everywhere come home through the evening smoke

meaning.en: Mao's picture of a bumper harvest in Shaoshan: crops rolling like waves and workers returning at dusk.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东写家乡韶山丰收景象：庄稼如千重浪涌，劳动者在暮色炊烟中归来。

equivalents: fields rolling like waves at harvest

examples.zh: 秋收时节，满眼是“喜看稻菽千重浪，遍地英雄下夕烟”的景象。
examples.en: At harvest time the view is of 'glad to see rice and beans in waves a thousand deep'.

examples.zh: 新闻稿用“喜看稻菽千重浪，遍地英雄下夕烟”来形容丰收。
examples.en: The news report used 'rice and beans in waves a thousand deep, heroes everywhere returning through evening smoke' to describe the harvest.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'Arriving at Shaoshan' (《七律·到韶山》) in June 1959, on visiting his home village after 32 years.
story.zh: 毛泽东1959年6月时隔三十二年回故乡韶山，作《七律·到韶山》。

usage.en: Quoted of bumper harvests. 稻菽 means rice and beans (grains); 重 is chóng (layer). Mao wrote it on his return to Shaoshan in 1959.
usage.zh: 多用于形容丰收。“稻菽”指稻和豆，泛指粮食；“重”读 chóng。毛泽东1959年回韶山时所作。

text: 飒爽英姿五尺枪，曙光初照演兵场；中华儿女多奇志，不爱红装爱武装
pinyin: sà shuǎng yīng zī wǔ chǐ qiāng, shǔ guāng chū zhào yǎn bīng chǎng, zhōng huá ér nǚ duō qí zhì, bù ài hóng zhuāng ài wǔ zhuāng
literal: bold · dashing · heroic · bearing · five-foot · rifle, dawn · light · first · shines · drill · soldier · ground, Chinese · sons · daughters · many · extraordinary · ambitions, not · love · red · attire · love · military · gear
natural: a dashing, heroic bearing with a five-foot rifle, dawn lighting the drill ground; China's daughters have great ambitions, preferring uniforms to rouge

meaning.en: Mao's quatrain on a photograph of a woman militia member: women of China prefer military uniform to fine clothes.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东为女民兵照片题的七绝：中华女儿胸怀大志，不爱红妆爱武装。

equivalents: women who prefer uniform to finery

examples.zh: 她穿着军装，照片旁写着“飒爽英姿五尺枪，曙光初照演兵场；中华儿女多奇志，不爱红装爱武装”。
examples.en: She wore a uniform, and beside her photo were the words 'not fond of finery, fond of arms'.

examples.zh: 纪念展览里挂着“飒爽英姿五尺枪，曙光初照演兵场；中华儿女多奇志，不爱红装爱武装”的题诗。
examples.en: The exhibition displayed the whole poem 'a dashing, heroic bearing…'.

origin.source: 毛泽东《七绝·为女民兵题照》（1961年）

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote this quatrain, 'Inscribed on a Photograph of Women Militia' (《七绝·为女民兵题照》), in February 1961.
story.zh: 毛泽东1961年2月题写此七绝，题在女民兵照片上。

usage.en: The last line 不爱红装爱武装 is widely quoted alone for women in uniform and in debates on gender. 飒爽 is sà shuǎng.
usage.zh: 末句“不爱红装爱武装”常单独引用，用于谈论女性从军或性别话题。“飒爽”读 sà shuǎng。

pinyin: tuán jié, jǐn zhāng, yán sù, huó pō

meaning.en: The motto of the Counter-Japanese Military and Political University (抗大): unity, urgency, discipline and spirited vitality.
meaning.zh: 抗日军事政治大学（抗大）的校训：团结、紧张、严肃、活泼。

equivalents: work hard, play hard
a spirit of unity and energy

examples.zh: 抗大校训是“团结，紧张，严肃，活泼”。
examples.en: The motto of Kangda was 'united, intense, earnest, lively'.

examples.zh: 班主任把“团结，紧张，严肃，活泼”写在黑板上，作为班级的目标。
examples.en: The class teacher wrote 'united, intense, earnest, lively' on the blackboard as the class's goal.

origin.source: 抗日军事政治大学校训（1930年代）

story.en: The Counter-Japanese Military and Political University (抗大), founded in Yan'an in 1936–37, adopted these four words as its motto; they are commonly associated with Mao Zedong's guidance of the school.
story.zh: 抗日军事政治大学（抗大）创办于1936—37年的延安，以这四个词为校训，一般认为与毛泽东对该校的指导有关。

usage.en: Often quoted as a style of work and study, and as the old motto of a school. It is commonly credited to Mao Zedong's guidance of the university in the late 1930s; the exact wording and date of his formulation are not settled here, so the origin names the school motto itself.
usage.zh: 常作学风、工作作风的概括，也是一所学校的旧校训。一般认为出自毛泽东在1930年代后期对抗大的指导；其具体措辞与提出时间此处不作断定，因此出处只写校训本身。

text: 此去泉台招旧部，旌旗十万斩阎罗
pinyin: cǐ qù quán tái zhāo jiù bù, jīng qí shí wàn zhǎn yán luó
literal: this · going · Springs · Terrace · summon · old · troops, banners · ten thousand · slay · King Yama
natural: going now to the Nine Springs I will rally my old troops; with a hundred thousand banners we shall slay Yama

meaning.en: Chen Yi's defiant verse written in expectation of death: even in the underworld he will gather his comrades and fight.
meaning.zh: 陈毅在预料牺牲时所写的豪迈诗句：即使到了阴间，也要召集旧部，继续战斗。

equivalents: defiant even in the face of death

examples.zh: 陈毅在梅岭写下“此去泉台招旧部，旌旗十万斩阎罗”，视死如归。
examples.en: On Meiling Chen Yi wrote 'I go to the Springs to rally my old troops, ten thousand banners to slay Yama', facing death unafraid.

examples.zh: 读到“此去泉台招旧部，旌旗十万斩阎罗”，同学们都深受感动。
examples.en: Reading 'going to the Springs to rally my old troops…', the students were deeply moved.

story.en: Chen Yi wrote the three poems 'Meiling Three Chapters' (《梅岭三章》) in late 1936 when besieged in the Meiling mountains, expecting to be killed; this is the end of the first.
story.zh: 陈毅1936年冬被围困梅山（梅岭），自料难免，作《梅岭三章》；此为第一首结尾。

usage.en: 泉台 is the underworld; 阎罗 is Yama, king of the dead. Quoted to express fearlessness before death and a revolutionary spirit.
usage.zh: “泉台”指阴间，“阎罗”即阎罗王。用来表达视死如归、革命到底的气概。

text: 投身革命即为家，血雨腥风应有涯；取义成仁今日事，人间遍种自由花
pinyin: tóu shēn gé mìng jí wéi jiā, xuè yǔ xīng fēng yīng yǒu yá, qǔ yì chéng rén jīn rì shì, rén jiān biàn zhòng zì yóu huā
literal: throw · self · into revolution · is · be · home, blood · rain · fishy · wind · should · have · limit, take · righteousness · accomplish · humaneness · today's · task, human world · everywhere · plant · freedom · flowers
natural: to give oneself to the revolution is to be at home; the storm of blood must have an end; to die for righteousness is today's task, to sow flowers of freedom through the world

meaning.en: Chen Yi's third Meiling poem: giving oneself to the cause as home, accepting sacrifice, and sowing freedom.
meaning.zh: 陈毅《梅岭三章》其三：以革命为家，血雨腥风终有尽头，今日舍生取义，要让人间遍开自由之花。

equivalents: sow the flowers of freedom
give one's life for a cause

examples.zh: “投身革命即为家，血雨腥风应有涯；取义成仁今日事，人间遍种自由花”，是陈毅留给同志们的诗句。
examples.en: 'Dying for righteousness is today's task, to sow flowers of freedom through the world' is what Chen Yi left to his comrades.

examples.zh: 语文课上，老师讲解了“投身革命即为家，血雨腥风应有涯；取义成仁今日事，人间遍种自由花”。
examples.en: In Chinese class the teacher explained 'to give oneself to the revolution is to be at home; the storm of blood must have an end'.

story.en: The third of Chen Yi's 'Meiling Three Chapters', written in 1936 while hiding in the mountains of the Jiangxi–Guangdong border.
story.zh: 陈毅《梅岭三章》第三首，1936年隐蔽于赣粤边山区时所作。

usage.en: The third of 《梅岭三章》. 取义成仁 echoes Confucius' 杀身成仁 and Mencius' 舍生取义. 血 is xuè in 血雨腥风; 种 is zhòng. Quoted in memorial and patriotic contexts.
usage.zh: 《梅岭三章》第三首。“取义成仁”呼应孔子“杀身成仁”、孟子“舍生取义”。“血雨腥风”的“血”读 xuè，“种”读 zhòng。多用于纪念和爱国教育场合。

text: 攻城不怕坚，攻书莫畏难；科学有险阻，苦战能过关
pinyin: gōng chéng bù pà jiān, gōng shū mò wèi nán, kē xué yǒu xiǎn zǔ, kǔ zhàn néng guò guān
literal: attack · city · not · fear · strong, attack · books · don't · dread · hard, science · has · perilous · obstacles, bitter · fight · can · pass · the pass
natural: do not fear a strong city when attacking it; do not dread difficulty when attacking books; science has its perils, but hard struggle will break through

meaning.en: Ye Jianying's verse urging hard study: tackle books and science with the same courage as a siege.
meaning.zh: 叶剑英的诗，勉励人们攻读与科研：像攻城一样不畏艰难，苦战必能过关。

equivalents: study as you would storm a fortress
hard work breaks through every barrier

examples.zh: 老师把“攻城不怕坚，攻书莫畏难；科学有险阻，苦战能过关”写在教室墙上。
examples.en: The teacher wrote 'attacking a city, fear not its strength; attacking books, dread not the difficulty' on the classroom wall.

examples.zh: 研究生开题时，导师送给他一句话：“攻城不怕坚，攻书莫畏难；科学有险阻，苦战能过关。”
examples.en: At his thesis proposal the supervisor gave him one line: 'science has its perils, but hard struggle will break through'.

story.en: Ye Jianying (1897-1986), a Marshal of the PLA, wrote the quatrain 'Storming the Pass' (《攻关》) to encourage the study of science.
story.zh: 叶剑英（1897—1986）元帅作七绝《攻关》，勉励人们攻读科学。

usage.en: Often quoted to students and researchers as encouragement; 攻关 is also a set term for tackling a key technical problem. The poem was written in the late 1970s and became well known when science and education were being revived.
usage.zh: 常用来勉励学生和科研人员；“攻关”也是集中力量解决关键技术难题的固定说法。此诗写于1970年代后期，在科学教育重振时广为流传。

pinyin: lǚ duān dà shì bù hú tu
literal: Lü Duan · big · matters · not · muddled
natural: Lü Duan is not muddled in great matters

meaning.en: Said of someone who may seem careless over trifles but stays clear-headed and firm on matters of principle.
meaning.zh: 形容人小事上或许不拘小节，遇到大事、原则问题却头脑清醒、立场坚定。

equivalents: sharp when it matters
clear-headed on the big issues

examples.zh: 人们说他是吕端大事不糊涂，关键时刻从不含糊。
examples.en: People say he is like Lü Duan, never muddled in great matters, never wavering at the critical moment.

examples.zh: 老厂长平时不拘小节，但吕端大事不糊涂，重大决策从没出过错。
examples.en: The old director is easygoing in small things, but like Lü Duan he is clear in great ones and has never erred on a major decision.

story.en: When Emperor Taizong of Song wished to make Lü Duan chief minister, someone objected that Lü was muddle-headed. Taizong replied 'Duan is muddled in small matters, but not in great ones' (端小事糊涂，大事不糊涂) and appointed him. Lü later helped secure the succession of Emperor Zhenzong. Mao Zedong used the phrase of Ye Jianying.
story.zh: 宋太宗想任吕端为相，有人说吕端为人糊涂，太宗说：“端小事糊涂，大事不糊涂。”遂决意任命。后来吕端在真宗继位一事上起了关键作用。毛泽东曾以此语评叶剑英。

usage.en: Used as a compliment. The Song emperor's remark was 端小事糊涂，大事不糊涂 ("Duan is muddled in small matters, not in great ones"). Mao Zedong applied the phrase to Marshal Ye Jianying, which made it well known in modern politics. 糊涂 is hú tu.
usage.zh: 作褒义。宋太宗原话是“端小事糊涂，大事不糊涂”。毛泽东曾以此评价叶剑英元帅，使这句话在近现代更为人知。“糊涂”读 hú tu。
